ASM-01-asm0-setup-and-tooling-supplement.content:
# A definition that the linker cannot see

This optional setup transfer activity follows the required mixed C/assembly
project. Identify the boundary between assembling a function and making that
function available to another object file. Keep this activity's learner and
reference work separate from the required setup attempt.

## Read the object boundary

The C caller declares `lab_answer` and expects its implementation in another
object. The assembly file contains that label, but its learner version omits
the global-binding directive. An assembler can produce a valid object with a
local function symbol while a separate C object still has an unresolved global
reference. Successful assembly therefore does not establish successful linking.

GNU assembly's `.globl lab_answer` makes this definition available to the linker
outside its own object. It does not change the function's return instruction or
invent a second implementation. On Linux x86-64 using the System V AMD64 ABI,
this small function returns an integer through EAX. The supplied routine does
not allocate a stack frame or modify callee-saved registers; `ret` consumes the
caller's return address.

The source uses GNU AT&T notation: `movl $LAB_VALUE, %eax` writes a
32-bit immediate into EAX, with the source operand first. The guide's Intel
disassembly view puts the destination first: the completed default instruction
is `mov eax,0x2a`. These are two renderings of the same emitted instruction.

## Environment and files

Use an owned Linux x86-64 VM or WSL environment with CMake 3.20+, GCC or Clang,
and binutils (`nm`, `readelf`, `objdump`). This pack uses ELF symbols and GNU
assembly syntax. The browser workspace edits and exports the files; native
building and object inspection take place in that Linux environment.

Each role contains `main.c`, `routine.S`, `lab.h`, `tests.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`
and `trace.md`. The shared README is this full guide. The C caller prints the
returned integer and checks it against the configured value. The contract
program supplies a separate caller; the worksheet records the build evidence.

## Predict and retain the unfinished build

From the exported project root, configure and build the learner role:

```sh
cc --version
cmake -S starter -B build-symbols-first -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang
cmake --build build-symbols-first --verbose
```

The initial link fails on the missing externally visible `lab_answer` definition.
Keep that diagnostic. GCC can be used by changing both compiler options to
`gcc` and selecting another build directory. Replace `clang` with `gcc` in the
direct stage commands as well. Do not repair the C caller or add
a second C implementation to hide the missing assembly definition.

Inspect the stages separately from the learner role directory:

```sh
cd starter
mkdir object-first
clang -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -c main.c -o object-first/main.o
clang -c routine.S -o object-first/routine.o
nm -P object-first/main.o
nm -P object-first/routine.o
readelf -Ws object-first/routine.o
objdump -dr -Mintel object-first/routine.o
clang object-first/main.o object-first/routine.o -o object-first/app
```

The last command reproduces the link failure. Compare the caller's undefined
symbol with the routine's local function definition. In GNU `nm` output,
lowercase `t` identifies a local text symbol and uppercase `T` a global text
symbol. Use the `readelf` binding column as a second view. Record the actual
symbol spelling and raw diagnostic instead of assuming every undefined-symbol
error has this cause.

## Make one directive repair

Replace the TODO comment in `routine.S` with `.globl lab_answer`, leaving the
function body and caller unchanged. From the project root, use a fresh build:

```sh
cmake -S starter -B build-symbols-fixed -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang
cmake --build build-symbols-fixed --verbose
ctest --test-dir build-symbols-fixed --output-on-failure
./build-symbols-fixed/app
```

The default output is `answer=42`. Repeat the object inspection and compare the
same function's global binding with the original local binding. Explain why the
link result changed while the return instruction kept the same purpose.

Configure another fresh build with `-DLAB_VALUE=73`, then run and test it. The
output becomes `answer=73`; this changes the configured return value and leaves
the object-boundary explanation intact. Values outside 0 through 255 are refused
by the supplied configuration. Keep compiler, role and configuration changes
separate in the worksheet.

## Completion and review

Complete `trace.md` with the failed link, both object symbol views, the minimal
repair, successful native output and changed-value run. Compare the reference
only after recording an independent diagnosis. Its only role-specific source
change is the global-binding directive. Code checks do not complete the worksheet.

If linking still fails, retain the exact command and check which object defines
the requested spelling, whether that definition is global, and whether that
object was included. A stale build or a differently named function is a separate
case. Retain separate fresh build directories and record each command's status.
An older executable does not prove that changed source compiled and linked
successfully.

References: [GNU symbol visibility](https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/as/Global.html)
and [GCC compilation stages](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Overall-Options.html).

#include "lab.h"
.text
.p2align 2
# TODO: export lab_answer to the separately compiled C caller
.type lab_answer, @function
lab_answer:
    movl $LAB_VALUE, %eax
    ret
.size lab_answer, .-lab_answer
.section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits

#ifndef SETUP_LAB_H
#define SETUP_LAB_H
#ifndef LAB_VALUE
#define LAB_VALUE 42
#endif
#ifndef __ASSEMBLER__
_Static_assert(LAB_VALUE >= 0 && LAB_VALUE <= 255, "LAB_VALUE range");
int lab_answer(void);
#endif
#endif

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(SetupEvidence LANGUAGES C ASM)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF)
set(CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS ON)
set(LAB_VALUE 42 CACHE STRING "Integer returned by the owned assembly function")
if(NOT LAB_VALUE MATCHES "^[0-9]+$" OR LAB_VALUE GREATER 255)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "LAB_VALUE must be an integer from 0 through 255")
endif()

enable_testing()
foreach(program IN ITEMS app contracts)
    if(program STREQUAL "app")
        set(caller main.c)
    else()
        set(caller tests.c)
    endif()
    add_executable(${program} ${caller} routine.S)
    target_compile_definitions(${program} PRIVATE LAB_VALUE=${LAB_VALUE})
    target_compile_options(${program} PRIVATE "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:-Wall;-Wextra;-Wpedantic;-Werror>")
endforeach()
add_test(NAME configured_function_value COMMAND contracts)

ASM-02-asm0-setup-and-tooling-supplement.content:
# Assembly input language and preprocessing evidence

This optional setup extension follows the required toolchain project. Diagnose
a build that sends preprocessor-dependent assembly directly to the assembler.
Keep its own learner and reference attempts separate from the required setup
project and the symbol-visibility transfer activity.

## Follow the selected input language

The supplied `routine.S` includes `lab.h` and uses the `LAB_VALUE` macro as an
immediate operand. An uppercase `.S` filename normally selects assembly with
preprocessing. The compiler driver's explicit `-x` option overrides suffix-based
language selection. The learner CMake configuration deliberately selects
`assembler`; the reference selects `assembler-with-cpp`.

With preprocessing disabled, the include directive is treated as an assembly
comment and the macro name remains unresolved. This can still produce an
object with a relocation against `LAB_VALUE`, followed by a link failure. The
stage that reports a failure need not be the stage where the wrong choice was
made. Here `lab_answer` is already global in both roles, so adding another
global directive does not resolve the macro.

The source uses GNU AT&T notation: `$` marks an immediate and `%eax` names
the 32-bit destination register. After preprocessing, `movl $41, %eax` appears
as `mov eax,0x29` in the guide's Intel disassembly view. Source and destination
order differ between the two notations; the emitted instruction is the same.

## Environment and files

Use an owned Linux x86-64 VM or WSL environment, CMake 3.20+, GCC or Clang and
binutils (`nm`, `readelf`, `objdump`). The source uses ELF and GNU assembly
syntax. Building and object inspection take place in that environment; the
browser workspace edits, saves and exports the project.

Each role contains `main.c`, `routine.S`, `lab.h`, `tests.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`
and `trace.md`, plus the shared complete README. The header defines a default
value and a C declaration guarded from assembly input. The C caller prints the
actual return value; the second caller tests it. No Python programming is needed.

## Observe the original selection

From the exported project root:

```sh
cmake -S starter -B build-language-first -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang
cmake --build build-language-first --verbose
```

Keep the failing diagnostic and the actual command compiling `routine.S`.
The learner cache selects `LAB_ASM_LANGUAGE=assembler`. Examine
`build-language-first/compile_commands.json` to find that explicit language
argument. Use another directory when selecting GCC instead of Clang.

From the learner role directory, compare the stages directly:

```sh
cd starter
mkdir language-first
clang -E -P -x assembler-with-cpp routine.S -o language-first/preprocessed.s
clang -x assembler -c routine.S -o language-first/raw.o
nm -P language-first/raw.o
readelf -r language-first/raw.o
objdump -dr -Mintel language-first/raw.o
clang -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -c main.c -o language-first/main.o
clang language-first/main.o language-first/raw.o -o language-first/app
```

The final link fails. Read the actual preprocessed text, unresolved macro symbol
and relocation together. The routine's global function symbol is distinct from
the unresolved `LAB_VALUE` symbol. Preserve both instead of inferring a missing
function from an unspecified link error.

## Correct the language and rebuild

Change the learner CMake default for `LAB_ASM_LANGUAGE` to
`assembler-with-cpp`. Use a fresh directory because a CMake cache retains its
previously selected value. From the project root:

```sh
cmake -S starter -B build-language-fixed -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_ASM_COMPILER=clang
cmake --build build-language-fixed --verbose
ctest --test-dir build-language-fixed --output-on-failure
./build-language-fixed/app
```

The output is `answer=41`. Compare the executed compiler arguments, preprocessed
numeric operand and object relocation listing with the unfinished build. Explain
which observation supports the preprocessing diagnosis. The learner and reference
files differ only in this default input-language selection.

Configure another fresh build with `-DLAB_VALUE=73`. Its output is `answer=73`.
Compare the changed numeric operand and successful native result while leaving
the selected preprocessing language fixed. Values outside 0 through 255 are
refused by the supplied configuration.

## Completion and troubleshooting

Complete `trace.md` with predictions, the original failing build, actual compiler
arguments, preprocessed text, object symbols/relocations, the minimal configuration
repair and the changed-value run. Compare the reference after making an independent
diagnosis. Passing code tests does not finish the worksheet.

If a changed source default appears ineffective, inspect the actual CMake cache
and commands and choose a new build directory. If preprocessing succeeds but the
link still fails, examine the remaining symbol and object-file evidence separately.
Do not use an older executable as the result of a build that failed.

References: [GCC input languages and stages](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Overall-Options.html)
and [CMake per-source compile options](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/prop_sf/COMPILE_OPTIONS.html).

.text
.p2align 2
.globl lab_answer
.type lab_answer, @function
lab_answer:
    movl $LAB_VALUE, %eax
    ret
.size lab_answer, .-lab_answer
.section .note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits

#ifndef SETUP_LAB_H
#define SETUP_LAB_H
#ifndef LAB_VALUE
#define LAB_VALUE 41
#endif
#ifndef __ASSEMBLER__
_Static_assert(LAB_VALUE >= 0 && LAB_VALUE <= 255, "LAB_VALUE range");

#endif
#endif

endif()

set_source_files_properties(routine.S PROPERTIES COMPILE_OPTIONS "-x;${LAB_ASM_LANGUAGE}")
enable_testing()
foreach(program IN ITEMS app contracts)
    if(program STREQUAL "app")
        set(caller main.c)
    else()
        set(caller tests.c)
    endif()

    target_compile_definitions(${program} PRIVATE LAB_VALUE=${LAB_VALUE})
    target_compile_options(${program} PRIVATE "$<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:-Wall;-Wextra;-Wpedantic;-Werror>")
endforeach()
